domain: Political Philosophy / Constitutional Theory / Legitimacy Studies
topic_summary: Analysis of the contested sovereign-legitimacy kernel: whether the right to rule derives from inherited status (monarchical reading) or delegated popular consent (republican reading). This is a foundational authority-grounding contest that has structured constitutional development across centuries, with different readings producing incompatible constraint structures around succession, accountability, and the locus of sovereignty.

key_entities: Hereditary Monarchy (dynastic succession system grounding authority in bloodline)
Constitutional Monarchy (hybrid form retaining symbolic monarch with parliamentary constraint)
Republic (delegated authority system grounding legitimacy in popular consent)
Social Contract Tradition (Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau - consent-based legitimation)
Parliamentary Systems (institutional constraint on monarchical power)
Marsilius of Padua / Defensor Pacis (early republican theorist, 1324)
key_tensions: Divine ordination vs popular consent as source of authority
Inherited privilege vs delegated mandate as legitimation principle
Traditional continuity vs democratic reform as governing logic
key_mechanisms: Dynastic succession (bloodline determines ruler; contested succession produces warfare)
Electoral delegation (citizens authorize representatives; officials removable via vote/recall)
Constitutional constraint (parliamentary limits on monarchical discretion in hybrid systems)
key_absences: Non-Western legitimation frameworks (Mandate of Heaven, Islamic caliphate models, African ubuntu-based authority)
Post-colonial legitimacy crises (imposed European state forms vs indigenous authority structures)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The sovereign-legitimacy kernel: the shared commitment that political authority requires justification, but contested on whether that justification derives from inherited status or delegated consent
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Monarchical reading: authority grounded in tradition, divine sanction, bloodline continuity. Republican reading: authority grounded in popular sovereignty, electoral mandate, constitutional delegation

readings.commitment: Authority derives from inherited status, sanctioned by tradition and divine ordination
readings.authority_grounding: Traditional authority (Weber) + divine right theology + dynastic continuity
readings.expected_structural_delta: Succession by bloodline; accountability to God/tradition not electorate; beneficiary=dynastic_lineage; victim=excluded_commoners; high ε (0.65+) due to non-removability of monarch

readings.commitment: Authority derives from delegated popular consent, revocable by the governed
readings.authority_grounding: Social contract theory (Locke, Rousseau) + popular sovereignty doctrine + electoral mechanisms
readings.expected_structural_delta: Succession by election; accountability to electorate; beneficiary=citizenry; victim=none (in theory) or excluded_non-citizens (in practice); moderate ε (0.35-0.50) due to electoral removability but institutional inertia

readings.commitment: Authority bifurcated: symbolic continuity via hereditary monarch, operational legitimacy via parliamentary delegation
readings.authority_grounding: Negotiated settlement between monarchical tradition and liberal reform (historical compromise)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Dual legitimation structure; monarch as symbolic anchor, parliament as policy authority; beneficiary=both_crown_and_parliament; victim=absolutist_factions_on_both_sides; low ε (0.20-0.30) due to institutional flexibility but symbolic lock-in

axiom_contradictions.basis: Monarchical axiom (authority inheres in bloodline, non-revocable by subjects) and republican axiom (authority delegated by consent, revocable by governed) cannot coexist in a single coherent framework. Accepting republican axiom as true requires rejecting the monarchical claim that inherited status grounds legitimate rule independent of popular will.

axes.structural_delta: Authority grounded in bloodline succession, divine sanction, and traditional continuity rather than popular mandate
axes.primary_observable: Succession mechanism (hereditary vs electoral); constitutional provisions on monarch's divine right or traditional status; removal mechanisms (none vs impeachment/recall)
axes.selection_reason: Core reading of contested kernel; highest ε; distinct beneficiary/victim structure from republican reading

axes.structural_delta: Authority grounded in popular consent, delegated via electoral mechanisms, revocable by the governed
axes.primary_observable: Electoral systems; constitutional provisions on popular sovereignty; accountability mechanisms (impeachment, recall, term limits)
axes.selection_reason: Core reading of contested kernel; axiom-contradictory to monarchical reading; different ε and constraint type

axes.structural_delta: Dual legitimation: hereditary monarch provides symbolic continuity, elected parliament provides operational authority
axes.primary_observable: Constitutional provisions bifurcating ceremonial vs policy powers; historical compromise documents (e.g., English Bill of Rights 1689)
axes.selection_reason: Hybrid reading demonstrating licensed plurality; lower ε but structurally distinct mechanism (bifurcation vs unitary authority)

axes.structural_delta: Monarchical succession rules produce chronic violent conflict when bloodline claims are ambiguous or contested
axes.primary_observable: Historical frequency of succession wars (Wars of the Roses, Spanish Succession, etc.); constitutional provisions for succession dispute resolution
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: downstream consequence of monarchical reading rather than independent axis; captured in monarchical constraint story as affects_constraint

axes.structural_delta: Republican systems exhibit gap between formal electoral accountability and actual responsiveness to popular will
axes.primary_observable: Policy-preference divergence studies; voter turnout rates; recall/impeachment frequency vs public dissatisfaction metrics
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: internal critique of republican reading but lower structural priority than core kernel readings; omega material on republican extractiveness

deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Downstream consequence of monarchical reading; captured as affects_constraint in monarchical constraint story rather than independent axis

omegas.description: Absence of non-Western legitimation frameworks (Mandate of Heaven, Islamic caliphate, African ubuntu-based authority). Are these genuinely different readings of the sovereign-legitimacy kernel, or distinct kernels entirely? If distinct, the kernel itself may be a Western construct.

Post-colonial states inherit European constitutional forms (monarchy or republic) imposed over indigenous authority structures. Does this produce a third reading (syncretic legitimacy) or a legitimacy vacuum? Deferred axis candidate.

Republican reading claims beneficiary=citizenry, but electoral_accountability_gap axis suggests political_class as actual beneficiary. Is republican legitimacy a rope (coordination) or snare (extraction masked as delegation)? Deferred axis electoral_accountability_gap explores this.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + deferred axis electoral_accountability_gap

omegas.description: Constitutional hybrid reading classified as scaffold (low ε, institutional flexibility). But UK/Spain/Japan stability vs Thailand/Morocco instability suggests ε may vary by implementation. Is this one reading or multiple?

Monarchical and republican readings hold axiom-contradictory positions (inherited vs delegated authority), yet constitutional hybrid reading demonstrates both can coexist institutionally. Does this invalidate the axiom contradiction, or does the hybrid reading constitute a third axiom (bifurcated authority) that sidesteps rather than resolves the contradiction?
